A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModuSeg work, and their text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, both end with references and omit the supplementary material they cite, limiting comparison of supplementary analyses and experimental details.

before.justification: v1 reports original VOC/COCO segmentation results, component ablations, oracle experiments, data-efficiency analyses and computational measurements in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports ADE20K and Cityscapes evaluations in Table 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same mask filtering, SBP, SMFA, prototype purification, proposal generation, retrieval voting and conflict resolution procedures. The added explanation that M denotes the proposal count clarifies existing notation.

E1.justification: Table 5 extends actual evaluation from VOC and COCO to ADE20K and Cityscapes, adding scene-parsing and urban-scene benchmark coverage. Both CorrCLIP-based and Mask Adapter-based configurations are evaluated on the added datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets in Tables 1, 2 and 7 and the component comparisons are retained. Table 5 extends the existing CorrCLIP and Mask Adapter comparisons to additional datasets; SEPL is newly discussed in related work but is not added to a reported evaluation.

E3.justification: The disclosed VOC/COCO split sizes, mIoU metric, backbone, erosion settings, rejection fraction and retrieval settings remain unchanged. ADE20K/Cityscapes results lack split, preprocessing and dataset-specific evaluation details, and the referenced supplementary material is unavailable, preventing a reliable assessment of protocol additions.

E4.justification: After matching the relocated tables, the reported component, backbone, proposer, oracle and data-efficiency analyses are unchanged. v3 newly references per-category SBP and interpretability analyses in supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs, so their addition or revision cannot be verified.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added benchmark results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds comparative results on two new benchmarks. On ADE20K/Cityscapes, CorrCLIP Direct scores 28.6/51.6 versus 44.7/66.0 with ModuSeg; Mask Adapter Direct scores 38.2/55.0 versus 45.6/64.2 with ModuSeg. These are newly reported results, while all existing VOC/COCO, ablation, oracle and efficiency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the cluster assumption and the mathematical definitions of purification, retrieval, voting and rasterization are retained. Explaining the existing symbol M does not introduce a new mathematical assumption or result.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal methodological contributions and conclusion retain the claims of training-free decoupling, improved prototypes through SBP/SMFA and competitive segmentation performance. The revised third contribution names ADE20K and Cityscapes as additional support for the existing generalizability claim.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits its scope to fixed-category WSSS and acknowledges strong pretrained representations as an important source of gains. Sections 4.2 and 4.4 replace stronger attribution to decoupling itself and broad system-efficiency language with pipeline effectiveness and measured training-time/validation-performance statements.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit 512 × 512 input resolution and the VOC/COCO category counts from the experimental settings. Principal hyperparameters, FAISS configurations, RTX 3090 disclosure and code-access information remain. The omitted resolution does not establish an actual configuration change.

R1.justification: v3 adds SEPL and the ADE20K/Cityscapes references, expands discussion of SAM-based WSSS and clarifies its relationship to open-vocabulary segmentation. SSR's preprint-to-AAAI reference update concerns the same work; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of related work and experimental interpretation, revised analysis headings, an added notation explanation, expanded affiliation text and new acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and most methodological prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The backbone comparison moves from Table 5 left to Table 4 right, while the proposer comparison moves in the opposite direction. Table 5 gains ADE20K/Cityscapes columns, and Tables 2 and 6 move to later pages. All three figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 5 broadens empirical support, while the revised discussion more carefully states applicability, the contribution of pretrained models and the scope of efficiency measurements. These benefits are tempered by unspecified protocols for the new benchmarks, removal of the input-resolution disclosure and unavailable supplementary analyses. The visible changes provide a modest overall improvement in evidential breadth and interpretive precision.
